title: Fundraiser for Prairieland Political Prisoner Marciela Rueda
content:
Donate at 




https://www.gofundme.com/f/help-maricelas-family-while-she-fights-for-justice







On July 4th, during a protest at the Prairieland Detention Center in Alvarado, Tx Maricela Rueda was arrested for speaking out against the injustices of the immigrant detention system. She is currently incarcerated for taking a courageous stand in defense of dignity and justice. Maricela has always been a tireless advocate for human rights. Maricela is a mother, a daughter, a sister, and a loyal friend. Her arrest has left her family facing sudden and overwhelming challenges. Maricela’s young daughter is now without her mother’s daily love and care, and her family must also manage her estate and responsibilities while navigating the uncertainty ahead. We are asking for your support to help ease the financial strain during this heartbreaking time. All funds will go directly toward caring for her daughter and managing the urgent needs of her household. Thank you for standing in solidarity with Maricela and those who love her.

title: Bill Dunne Running Down the Walls reportback
content:
The agency of repression closed the yard for my contribution to RDTW, this weekend before the fall, 2026. The passage of time is revealing a rift between the concrete paving the small courtyards that remained open and the knees. The hamstrings and the ridiculously curved treadmills have a similar schism. So I rode an elliptical into the fray to Run Down the Walls. I let ’em have both legs three days and then again two days before the fall, 19 & 20 September. I had to do some slithering to access the venue the second day, but so it goes in life with big brother And the day before the fall, I write this report. Plus, I may have added one more means of motion to run down the walls: rowing. After my engagements on the ellipticals had ended, I wrestled the rowing machine to wring a few more gritty grains from the walls.







As my feet pushed ever forward and my arms aided and abetted, the elliptical didn’t carry me any where but figuratively. My forced presence in that physical moment, however, let me, made me, invited me me to notice the little drops of sweat hitting the concrete floor as they dripped off me. At first, just a few isolated individuals dotted the scuzzy gym floor–literal drops in the bucket, but without even a bucket. title: Benjamin Song Running Down the Walls 2026 statement
content:
Hey y’all, my name is Champagne. I was sentenced this year to 100 years for, in the words of the government “[being] the embodiment of Antifa.” Before my sentencing, I spoke the truth clearly and refused to be interrupted in court. I am not afraid. Even as violence rises all around me both inside and outside these walls. I am not afraid because the struggle remains the same. The great disasters and failures we face remain the same. 




Our duty, as Assata told us, remains the same. I know I am just one in a sea of us. We are strong. We are smart and capable. We are committed. We will think and love and win. We will care for and protect each other. We will speak and listen, connect and grow. The better world we struggle for is our duty and our birthright. I will continue to fight for it. We will win it together. Thank you, each and every one of you. I am so grateful for the work and support of the ABCF and events like RDTW. Thank you for supporting us, supporting this, supporting yourself. I will see you when we are all free!




Champagne Song

title: Malik Muhammad Running Down the Walls 2026 statement
content:
Listen to my words and hear my signal of distress. I’m not just writing a statement. It’s an SOS. I’m running out of gas. I’ve almost nothing left. We’re losing ground thinking what we’re doing is our best. The movement at this juncture is failing this test.




If all we have is this cycle of our people taking action, then facing the brunt of state-sanctioned violence and hope for support during their time held hostage, it’s not enough. If we can muster money for lawyers to negotiate our surrender and get them rich, these agents of the state, this is no better. If paying the state millions for our people to survive inside and communicate with loved ones is our best, our imagination is stunted. We cannot limit ourselves to the confines of the box the state has given us. We cannot work with the ones causing the problem, No! We must do more, do better.




Reaching into hell and pulling those the state has damned from the depths. title: Bill Dunne Running Down the Walls 2026 statement
content:
SALUTATIONS AND FELICITATIONS TO MY RUNNING DOWN THE WALLS COMRADES!




Two tomorrows from the edge or another autumn here in the global north, we again lace up our moving gear. We shall run, walk, roll, hop, limp, down the barriers, obstacles, impediments, stumbling blocks, and sheer distance–for which we call out prison walls as a symbolic stand-in–between us and our literal and figurative destination. We may not reach that most equitable social reality in which all people will have the greatest possible freedom to develop their full human potential today. But we will unite across time and space and identity to make common progress for all the tomorrows that will come as we together run down the walls.




We will confront the apparatus of repression’s houses of steel and concrete and pain behind whose walls greed imprisons and tortures our friends, comrades, neighbors, relatives for the crimes of being here, wanting enough food, medicine, housing, security, education, seeking living wages for meaningful work. We will contest a predatory aristocracy’s imprisonment of our class brethren, sistren, nonconren within artificial national borders where that elite can more readily redistribute wealth upward and commit genocide against resisters’ communities. title: Brian DiPippa (Peppy) Running Down the Walls 2026 statement
content:
We have within us a strength, both personal and collective, that is capable of much more than we fear. It is okay to recognize fear; however afraid we may be, let us not cower.




Let us not look at empire for one day, but instead into your comrades eyes. Those eyes that know hunger, nay – famine! Those freedom eyes of a tiger so fixated on her target. Let’s go!




This year in celebration I join my partner Krystal and fellow veterans Marius Mason, Jessica Reznicek, Nikos Maziotis on the streets for the first time in many moons. We lick our paws from the wounds we have been dealt and we continue to proclaim the struggle for liberation.




We continue to act for freedom.

We continue to run down the walls.

We continue to remember our fallen.




May you feel as I have felt the whole period of incarceration — a thousand hands at my back and the ancestors in front of me who laid the path and broke trail with their efforts.




in solidarity,

-peppy

title: Oso Blanco Running Down the Walls 2026 statement
content:
Brothers and sisters in the struggle, this is Oso Blanco. I ask you to come out today to put your all into this 5k again this year. There is something that many of you need to know, if you don’t know already. Political prisoners throughout the system truly need your help in completing this 5k today because what you’re going to do is raise money that allows us to survive in these hell holes. It has become increasingly difficult to live in here — just to buy soap, toothpaste, and basic essentials has become prohibitively expensive and makes it difficult to survive in state and federal prisons and jails. Needless to say this is because this is a money making scheme; it’s all about profit, not justice in this industrial prison complex. I ask you to put forth your best effort today. You may feel tired, like giving up, but remember that we need you and we need your help in getting us out of these horrible places. I love you all. Oso Blanco 

https://freeosoblanco.org

title: Ronald Reed denied parole again.
content:

Board again denies parole for man convicted in 1970 murder of officer James Sackett Sr.




Minnesota’s Supervised Release Board has again denied parole to a man convicted in the ambush murder of St. Paul Police Officer James Sackett Sr. The board’s meeting on Friday marked the fourth time that Ronald Reed, 76, appealed for his release.




Julie Sackett was 14 months old on May 22, 1970 when a sniper’s bullet killed her father. She was too young to remember him.




“All I have is photos,” Sackett said in a phone interview with MPR News on Friday.




Officer Sackett had responded to an emergency call about a pregnant woman in distress at Hague Avenue and Victoria Street, about a half mile from the governor’s residence, but there was no emergency.




Investigators said that Ronald Reed had lain in wait with a .30-caliber rifle and fired at Sackett from across the street. Prosecutors said that Reed, who is Black, wanted to impress the national leadership of the Black Panthers by killing a white police officer.




The case sat dormant for decades until reporting by KSTP-TV led investigators to reopen it. In 2006, a Ramsey County jury 

convicted

 Reed of first-degree murder and conspiracy.
